modeling_assumptions.basis: Bellwether Point is a fictional site with no real zoning file to source. 250 ft clears a typical multi-story boardwalk roofline and dune-top tree line while remaining below both options' maximum rider height, so the comparison is not decided by construction.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing. The dwell time each option spends above this height, and therefore the scoring result, is sensitive to this value. See sensitivity_model.py FLEX.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Boarding-platform height above true ground datum, applied identically to both options
modeling_assumptions.basis: Large continuous-loading observation wheels board from a small raised platform, not bare ground; 2 m is a realistic, modest clearance.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Low. Applied identically to both options' midlines, so it does not by itself favor either option.

sensitivity_note: Primary metric (qualifying minutes per hour per meter of diameter) is sensitive to MA1 (the qualifying sightline height) and, jointly and identically, to MA2. See sensitivity_model.py and FACILITATOR.md.
_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC section 4
protagonist: Renata Koh, attractions engineer, Bellwether Point Pier Redevelopment Authority -- a former ride operator who went back to school for engineering and has designed sightlines for three sunset-view wheels without ever catching the view from one herself

deliverables.text: A height-versus-time function h(t) for each option, amplitude/midline/period labeled and justified.
A degrees-to-radians conversion table for each option's angular rotation rate.
A graph of each option's height function over one rotation with the qualifying height marked.
A worked inverse-trig solution finding the times height equals the qualifying height, and the resulting dwell interval.
A final scoring table: qualifying minutes/hour, and that total per meter of diameter, with a defended recommendation.

balance.argument_a: Option A's smaller diameter (120 m vs 158.5 m) means less structural material and foundation load per the authority's own capital-scale proxy. On the authority's actual scoring rule -- qualifying sunset-view minutes per operating hour, per meter of wheel diameter -- Option A scores higher than Option B: roughly 0.212 qualifying min/hr per meter of diameter for A versus roughly 0.197 for B, a real but modest edge.
balance.argument_b: Option B's much larger radius keeps every rider above the qualifying height for a longer share of each rotation and, combined with its larger cabin capacity, delivers more total qualifying sunset-view minutes per operating hour in absolute terms -- roughly 31.2 min/hr for B versus roughly 25.4 min/hr for A, an 18.5% edge in raw output that a Hero who never applies the authority's own per-diameter scoring rule will see as the whole story.
balance.margin_basis: margin_pct = 100*(effA-effB)/effA where effX = (qualifying dwell minutes per rotation for X) * (rotations per hour) / (diameter of X in meters), computed from D-series arithmetic in sensitivity_model.py evaluate().

derived.note: D1-D5 worked figures, computed by sensitivity_model.py evaluate()/raw_minutes(), recorded here so FACILITATOR.md's arithmetic is checkable against a value of record instead of drifting silently.

ui_slider_bounds.note: Pier Wheel - Interactive.html qualifying-height and boarding-clearance sliders use these as display-range maximums only -- arbitrary UI bounds, not case data.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: Bellwether Point is a fictional pier site with no real zoning file, roofline survey, or dune-height record to research -- the qualifying sightline height cannot be known in advance by any amount of research, the same irreducible-unknown character as a future price. Tier 2 probe P5 confirms this dial is genuinely load-bearing: at -50% (38.1 m) the margin widens to 21.9%, over the SPEC section 2 20% cap; at +50% (114.3 m) the winner flips to Option B and the margin (68.6%) also breaks the cap. Both directions are disclosed here and in case.json.modeling_assumptions MA1's own 'Load-bearing' sensitivity note and FACILITATOR.md's Sensitivity Note, not hidden. This is the case's single most load-bearing dial -- the base case's 76.2 m (250 ft) value was deliberately chosen to sit well below both options' maximum rider height so the comparison is not decided by construction, per MA1's basis, but the case's honest margin is genuinely sensitive to where within a defensible range that value is set.

Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; the 20:00-30:00 deep-conflict thread drops to a single thread (the scoring-rule read) instead of running raw-output and capital-efficiency as two separate threads.

No vote at Anchor 1 -- the Hero states an initial position instead. The guide plays devil's advocate directly, pushing the raw-total (Option B) reading before pointing back to Background's own scoring rule.
